text:
elena (PM): Heads-up — legal asked if we can offer SLA-triggered onboarding credits + a "breakglass" pin for high-risk customers requesting extra runway. thinking this should tie to acceptance gates, not ad-hoc.

sanjay (sales): Customer X pushed hard for pin exceptions last week. they want 90 days pinned and credits if we take them off earlier. can we standardize that?

amy (eng): We need clear bench criteria. if pinning bypasses our canary gates it increases regression risk. proposal: pin exceptions only if the cust passes a fast bench and signs a migration plan.

maria (solutions): +1. also require an instrumentation checklist (sample prompts + drift watch). otherwise ops load goes nuts.

elena (PM): Draft policy idea: (1) SLA credit formula (pct of committed throughput * days pinned), (2) mandatory smokebench within 48h, (3) migration runway with milestones. thoughts?

gabe (platform): Implementation note: platform can enforce smokebench and automated TTL for pins. but we need a human approval workflow for exceptions. ops-bot can log approvals.

ops-bot: auto: created approval request #PK-342 for pin exception (customer X). approver: @amy. link: https://rbwrd/approvals/PK-342

amy (eng): I can review. quick checklist from eng: 
- perf baseline (p95 < 300ms)
- token cost within 15% of catalog model
- sample eval set pass rate >= 90%
If all true we allow temporary pin.

sanjay (sales): Customers will haggle on the credit amount. can we provide a simple table in our SOW template? e.g., 7-day credit per 30 pinned days for enterprise, 3-day for mid-market.

elena (PM): Good idea — make it prescriptive so AE's don't negotiate wildly. need finance sign-off on numbers. @gabe can platform surface a per-tenant credit estimate?

gabe (platform): yes, we can calculate estimated token-days and present an estimated credit. will need schema from finance.

maria (solutions): Also add a deprecation clause: pinned models get a mandatory migration date no later than 180 days, with checkpoints at 30/90/150. helps reduce long-tail technical debt.

amy (eng): For the smokebench we should run both perf and quality probes. small script idea: 
```
# smokebench steps
run_bench --model pinned_variant --seqs sample_prompts.json --report perf,quality
if perf.p95 > 300ms -> fail
if quality.pass_rate < 90% -> fail
```
we can add this to the approval flow.

elena (PM): Action items: 
- elena: write policy draft + SOW credit table (due EOD Fri)
- gabe: prototype credit estimator + approval log hook (next week)
- amy: add smokebench script to infra repo and approval checklist (Weds)
- maria: draft migration milestones and comm templates (Thu)
- sanjay: collect top 3 customer asks/expected pushback and share (Tue)

sanjay (sales): I'll surface customer examples and their preferred credit language.

amy (eng): Quick question: should pinned models be excluded from automatic quantization/compaction? that affects cost & perf.

gabe (platform): They should be on a separate tunable lane. we can opt them out of certain infra optimizations while pinned, but it costs more. include that tradeoff in the SOW.

elena (PM): Perfect — let's reconvene Thu AM for a final PR on the policy. if anyone needs to add concerns earlier drop them here. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: reminder: meeting scheduled Thu 09:30 for pin-exception policy review.
